title: The Blackamoor
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Man once bought an Ethiopian slave, who had a black skin like all Ethiopians; but his new master thought his colour was due to his late owner's having neglected him, and that all he wanted was a good scrubbing. So he set to work with plenty of soap and hot water, and rubbed away at him with a will, but all to no purpose: his skin remained as black as ever, while the poor wretch all but died from the cold he caught.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what had the Man just bought at the start of the passage?
options: A team of oxen
An Ethiopian slave
A plot of farmland
A herd of sheep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the new master believe was the cause of the slave's colour?
options: A skin condition passed down in his family
The late owner's having neglected him
Long exposure to the sun
A disease he had caught at sea

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the master think the slave needed?
options: A good scrubbing
A change of clothes
A period of rest
A new set of tools

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the master use to scrub the slave?
options: Sand and vinegar
Plenty of soap and hot water
A rough brush and ash
Cold water and salt

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the result of all the scrubbing?
options: The slave's skin remained as black as ever
The slave's skin grew paler after a week
The slave's skin became irritated but changed colour
The scrubbing worked, but only in patches

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the slave besides his skin staying the same?
options: He nearly died from the cold he caught
He ran away from his new master
He fell ill from the soap
He lost his sense of hearing

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "neglected" mean in "his late owner's having neglected him"?
options: Praised excessively
Failed to care for properly
Trained rigorously
Introduced formally

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Effort spent trying to change what cannot be changed is wasted, and can even cause harm
Cleanliness always improves a person's health
New owners should never trust the word of a previous owner
Cold water is more effective than hot water for scrubbing

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what colour was the slave's skin?
options: Black
Deeply tanned
Pale
Grey

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the master go about trying to change the slave's colour?
options: He set to work with plenty of soap and hot water
He hired a physician to examine him
He kept him indoors away from sunlight
He fed him a special diet

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does it describe the effort spent scrubbing the slave?
options: As all to no purpose
As a complete success
As only partly effective
As too dangerous to continue

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "wretch" mean in "the poor wretch all but died"?
options: A pitiable, suffering person
A dishonest trickster
A skilled craftsman
A wealthy nobleman

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what mistaken assumption led the master to scrub the slave?
options: He believed the slave's colour was dirt caused by neglect rather than a natural trait
He believed the slave had recently painted his skin
He believed soap could cure any illness
He believed the slave wanted to be scrubbed

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A master scrubs his new slave to remove dirt he wrongly assumes is there, harming him without changing his natural colour
A slave scrubs himself clean to please his new master
A master discovers his slave was neglected and nurses him back to health
A slave's skin changes colour after a long illness
